comments.author: Matthew Coombs
comments.comment:
The autonomy jump is where most teams get burned.

A useful test before calling something an agent: can it recover from bad context, partial tool failure, and ambiguous user intent without silently making things worse?

If not, it is probably still a workflow with an LLM step, and that is fine.

comments.author: Sairam Sundaresan
comments.comment: The failure mode I worry about is that most eval setups treat the judge as a fixed measuring instrument, but in agent loops the judge is part of the system being acted on. A useful stress test is to log not just pass/fail, but verdict stability under paraphrase, adversarial disagreement, and multi-judge entropy. If a judge flips when challenged, I would rather route that case to human review than average it into a clean-looking score.
